content: Chloral hydrate is a sedative medication prescribed for short-term treatment of insomnia, helping individuals fall asleep and maintain sleep for adequate rest. It is also used to alleviate anxiety and induce sleep before surgical procedures. Additionally, it may be administered post-surgery for pain management and to treat symptoms of alcohol withdrawal. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Chloral hydrate is available in capsule and liquid forms for oral administration, as well as a suppository for rectal use. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take chloral hydrate exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. For the liquid form, mix it with half a glass of water, fruit juice, or ginger ale, and drink it immediately. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water or fruit juice; do not chew the capsule. If using the suppository, follow these steps: Remove the wrapper. Moisten the tip of the suppository with water. Lie on your left side and raise your right knee to your chest. (If you are left-handed, lie on your right side and raise your left knee.) Using your finger, insert the suppository into the rectum, approximately 1/2 to 1 inch for infants and children, and 1 inch for adults. Hold it in place for a few moments. Stand up after about 15 minutes. Wash your hands thoroughly and resume your normal activities. Chloral hydrate has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than instructed by your doctor. Continue taking chloral hydrate even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, especially if you have been using it in large doses or for an extended period. Your doctor will likely reduce your dose gradually. Before taking chloral hydrate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to chloral hydrate, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and drugs), or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), antihistamines, furosemide (Lasix), medications for depression or seizures, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, heart or stomach problems, a history of alcohol or drug abuse, or asthma. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking chloral hydrate, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking chloral hydrate. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication. Chloral hydrate may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take it with food or milk. If you miss a dose, do not take it when you remember. Skip the missed dose entirely and take the next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Chloral hydrate may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Drowsiness Upset stomach Vomiting Diarrhea If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Skin rash Itching Confusion Difficulty breathing Slow heartbeat Extreme tiredness If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store chloral hydrate in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Protect the liquid form from light and do not freeze it. Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. If you have diabetes, use TesTape or Clinistix to test your urine for sugar. Do not use Clinitest, as chloral hydrate can cause false results. Do not share this medication with anyone else. Chloral hydrate is a controlled substance, and prescriptions may only be refilled a limited number of times. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions.
